t.3.51.1: But Damayantī, having heard those words of the swan, O Bhārata, was from that time on no longer at ease, on account of Nala.
t.3.51.2: Then Damayantī became wholly absorbed in anxious thought, wretched, pale-faced and emaciated, and at that time she was given over entirely to sighing.
t.3.51.3: With her gaze turned upward, she became absorbed in brooding, looking like one bereft of her senses; never did she find delight in bed, in seat, or in any pleasure.
t.3.51.5: Then, O lord of men, the group of Damayantī's friends informed the lord of Vidarbha that Damayantī was not well.
t.3.51.4: She slept neither by night nor by day, crying “Alas, alas!” again and again. Her friends recognized from her gestures that she was unwell and in that condition.
t.3.51.6: Having heard that from the band of Damayantī's companions, King Bhīma pondered that very great matter concerning his own daughter.
t.3.51.7: That lord of the earth, seeing that his own daughter had reached the bloom of youth, saw as his own duty the svayaṃvara of Damayantī.
t.3.51.9: Having heard of Damayantī's svayaṃvara, all the lords of the earth, the kings, then came to Bhīma at Bhīma's command.
t.3.51.8: He summoned the kings of the earth, O lord of the people, saying, “O heroes, let this be witnessed at the svayaṃvara,” O lord.
t.3.51.11: At that very time, the two ancient, great-souled sages, best of seers, wandering about, went from here to the world of Indra.
t.3.51.10: Making the earth resound with the clamor of elephants, horses and chariots, they came with colorful garlands and ornaments, and with splendid, finely adorned troops.
t.3.51.12: Nārada and Parvata, those great-souled sages of mighty vows, entered the palace of the king of the gods, where they were received with great honour.
t.3.51.13: Having honored the two, the thousand-eyed lord then asked after their unfailing well-being, and also after their health in every respect.
t.3.51.14: Our welfare, O god, is complete in every respect, O lord; and throughout the whole world, O Maghavan, the kings are faring well, O mighty one.
t.3.51.15: Having heard Nārada's words, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra asked: “Those lords of the earth who know dharma, warriors who fight having abandoned all care for their lives…”
t.3.51.17: Where now are those heroic kṣatriyas? For I do not see them coming, those kings, my beloved guests.
t.3.51.16: Those who, never turning their backs, meet their death by the weapon when their time comes, for them this world is imperishable and grants every desire, just as it does for me.
t.3.51.18: Thus addressed by Śakra, Nārada replied: "Hear from me, O blessed lord, the reason why the kings are not seen."
t.3.51.19: The daughter of the king of Vidarbha, renowned as Damayantī, has surpassed in beauty all the women on earth.
t.3.51.20: Her svayaṃvara, O Śakra, will take place before long; kings and princes from every quarter are going there.
t.3.51.21: The kings, seeking her who has become the jewel of the world, longed for her above all, O slayer of Bala and Vṛtra.
t.3.51.22: But while this was being told, the guardians of the worlds, together with Agni, those foremost of immortals, came into the presence of the king of the gods.
t.3.51.23: Then they all heard that momentous speech of Nārada, and having heard it, they said in delight, "We too shall go!"
t.3.51.24: Then all of them, great king, with their retinues and their mounts, went toward the land of the Vidarbhas, where all the kings of the earth had gathered.
t.3.51.25: King Nala too, O son of Kuntī, having heard of the gathering of kings, came there with an undaunted spirit, devoted to Damayantī.
t.3.51.26: Then the gods saw Nala on the road, standing on the surface of the earth, like Manmatha himself standing there in bodily form, so rich was his beauty.
t.3.51.27: Seeing him shining like the sun, those guardians of the worlds stood still, their resolve gone, astonished at the splendour of his beauty.
t.3.51.28: Then the heaven-dwellers, halting their aerial chariots in the sky and descending from the vault of heaven, spoke to the Naiṣadha, O king.
t.3.51.29: O, O Naiṣadha, lord of kings, Nala, you are true to your vows! Give us your help; be our messenger, O best of men.
